import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.23

by V. D. Mazurov

Let $G$ be a finite group, $B$ a block of characters of $G$, $D(B)$ its defect group and
$k(B)$ (respectively, $k_0(B)$) the number of all irreducible complex characters (of height $0$)
lying in $B$. *Conjectures:*

a) (R. Brauer) $k(B) \leq |D(B)|$; this has been proved for $p$-soluble groups
(D. Gluck, K. Magaard, U. Riese, P. Schmid, *J. Algebra*, **279** (2004), 694–719);

b) (J. B. Olsson) $k_0(B) \leq |D(B) : D(B)'|$, where $D(B)'$ is the derived subgroup of
$D(B)$;

c) (R. Brauer) $D(B)$ is abelian if and only if $k_0(B) = k(B)$.

Part c) is Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture. It is not starred in the notebook, but it is now a
theorem: the direction "$D(B)$ abelian $\Rightarrow k_0(B) = k(B)$" was proved by Kessar and
Malle (2013), and the converse by Malle, Navarro, Schaeffer Fry and Tiep (2024). Parts a) and b)
are open.

## Formalisation

Here "block" means $p$-block for a prime $p$; the statements are quantified over $p$, $G$ and
$B$. Mathlib has no block theory, so this file sets up Brauer's character-theoretic definitions
(Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Chapter 15; Navarro, *Characters and Blocks of
Finite Groups*, Chapters 3 and 4). Let $\mathbf{R}$ be the ring of all algebraic integers in
$\mathbb{C}$ (`integralClosure ℤ ℂ`) and $M$ a maximal ideal of $\mathbf{R}$ containing $p$.

* The irreducible complex characters of $G$ are the characters of the simple objects of
  `FDRep ℂ G`.
* For an irreducible character $\chi$ and $x \in G$ with conjugacy class $K$, the central
  character value $\omega_\chi(\hat K) = |K| \chi(x) / \chi(1) = |G : C_G(x)| \chi(x) / \chi(1)$
  is an algebraic integer. Two irreducible characters $\chi, \psi$ lie in the same $p$-block if
  and only if $\omega_\chi(\hat K) \equiv \omega_\psi(\hat K) \pmod M$ for every conjugacy
  class $K$; the $p$-blocks are the equivalence classes of this relation. The resulting
  partition does not depend on the choice of $M$; the statements below quantify over all
  admissible $M$.
* A block $B$ has a central character $\lambda_B$ with $\lambda_B(\hat K) = \omega_\chi(\hat K)
  \bmod M$ for any $\chi \in B$. The defect groups of a class $K = x^G$ are the Sylow
  $p$-subgroups $\delta(K)$ of $C_G(x)$. By Brauer's min–max theorem, the defect groups of $B$
  are exactly the groups $\delta(K)$ of smallest order among the classes $K$ with
  $\lambda_B(\hat K) \neq 0$; they form a single conjugacy class of $p$-subgroups of $G$. This
  characterisation is taken as the definition of a defect group $D(B)$.
* If $|G|_p = p^a$ and $|D(B)| = p^d$, every $\chi \in B$ has $\chi(1)_p = p^{a - d + h}$ for an
  integer $h \geq 0$, the *height* of $\chi$. So $\chi$ has height $0$ if and only if
  $\chi(1)_p |D(B)| = |G|_p$.

Since all defect groups of $B$ are conjugate, $|D(B)|$, $|D(B) : D(B)'|$ and whether $D(B)$ is
abelian are well defined, and the statements quantify over every defect group of $B$. The solved
special case of a) for $p$-soluble groups is only mentioned in the docstring.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 9.23.
* D. Gluck, K. Magaard, U. Riese, P. Schmid, *The solution of the k(GV)-problem*,
  [J. Algebra 279 (2004), 694–719](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2004.02.027).
* R. Kessar, G. Malle, *Quasi-isolated blocks and Brauer's height zero conjecture*,
  [Ann. of Math. 178 (2013), 321–384](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2013.178.1.6).
* G. Malle, G. Navarro, A. A. Schaeffer Fry, P. H. Tiep, *Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture*,
  [Ann. of Math. 200 (2024), 557–608](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2024.200.2.4).
-/
open CategoryTheory
namespace Kourovka.«9.23»
section Definitions
variable {G : Type} [Group G]

blocks.code:
def IsIrreducibleCharacter (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ V : FDRep ℂ G, Simple V ∧ V.character = χ
blocks.docstring:
A function `χ : G → ℂ` is an irreducible complex character of `G` if it is the character
of a simple, i.e. irreducible, finite-dimensional complex representation of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FDRep.character together with CategoryTheory.Simple (used to define it)
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.23».IsIrreducibleCharacter
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has `FDRep.character` and `CategoryTheory.Simple` but no predicate 'χ is an irreducible character of G' on functions G → ℂ, which is needed to form blocks as sets of characters.

blocks.name: IsIrreducibleCharacter
blocks.text:
/-- A function `χ : G → ℂ` is an irreducible complex character of `G` if it is the character
of a simple, i.e. irreducible, finite-dimensional complex representation of `G`. -/
def IsIrreducibleCharacter (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ V : FDRep ℂ G, Simple V ∧ V.character = χ

blocks.code:
noncomputable def centralCharacter (χ : G → ℂ) (x : G) : ℂ :=
  ((Subgroup.centralizer {x}).index : ℂ) * χ x / χ 1
blocks.docstring:
The central character value $\omega_\chi(\hat K) = |K| \chi(x) / \chi(1)$ of `χ` at the
conjugacy class $K$ of `x`, where $|K| = |G : C_G(x)|$. For an irreducible character `χ` this is
an algebraic integer.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.centralizer / Subgroup.index (used for |K| = |G : C_G(x)|); nothing for ω_χ itself
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.23».centralCharacter
justification.why_needed: The central character values ω_χ(K̂) = |K|χ(x)/χ(1) are the basis of Brauer's definition of p-blocks; Mathlib has no central characters.

blocks.name: centralCharacter
blocks.text:
/-- The central character value $\omega_\chi(\hat K) = |K| \chi(x) / \chi(1)$ of `χ` at the
conjugacy class $K$ of `x`, where $|K| = |G : C_G(x)|$. For an irreducible character `χ` this is
an algebraic integer. -/
noncomputable def centralCharacter (χ : G → ℂ) (x : G) : ℂ :=
  ((Subgroup.centralizer {x}).index : ℂ) * χ x / χ 1
variable (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ))

blocks.code:
def idealImage : Set ℂ :=
  Subtype.val '' (M : Set (integralClosure ℤ ℂ))
blocks.docstring: The set of complex numbers lying in the ideal `M` of the ring of algebraic integers.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Ideal.map (not applicable: ℂ is a field), Subtype.val '' M (this is the definition).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.23».idealImage
justification.why_needed: The set of complex numbers lying in an ideal M of integralClosure ℤ ℂ; lets us write ω_χ(x) − ω_ψ(x) ∈ M without first proving that central character values are algebraic integers.

blocks.name: idealImage

blocks.code:
def SameBlock (χ ψ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : G, centralCharacter χ x - centralCharacter ψ x ∈ idealImage M
blocks.docstring:
`χ` and `ψ` lie in the same block with respect to the maximal ideal `M` of the algebraic
integers: $\omega_\chi(\hat K) \equiv \omega_\psi(\hat K) \pmod M$ for every conjugacy class
$K$ of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Ideal.Quotient / Ideal membership on integralClosure ℤ ℂ (used inside the definition)
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.23».SameBlock
justification.why_needed: Brauer's relation ω_χ ≡ ω_ψ (mod M) defining p-blocks; absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: SameBlock
blocks.text:
/-- `χ` and `ψ` lie in the same block with respect to the maximal ideal `M` of the algebraic
integers: $\omega_\chi(\hat K) \equiv \omega_\psi(\hat K) \pmod M$ for every conjugacy class
$K$ of `G`. -/
def SameBlock (χ ψ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : G, centralCharacter χ x - centralCharacter ψ x ∈ idealImage M

blocks.code:
def IsBlock (B : Set (G → ℂ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ χ, IsIrreducibleCharacter χ ∧ B = {ψ | IsIrreducibleCharacter ψ ∧ SameBlock M χ ψ}
blocks.docstring:
`B` is a block of characters of `G` with respect to the maximal ideal `M` (a $p$-block, where
$p$ is the prime in `M`): an equivalence class of irreducible characters of `G` under
`SameBlock M`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None (searched for block/defect/Brauer in Mathlib and the repo)
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.23».IsBlock
justification.why_needed: The notion of a p-block of characters of a finite group is absent from Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

blocks.name: IsBlock

blocks.code:
def IsNonvanishingClass (B : Set (G → ℂ)) (x : G) : Prop :=
  ∀ χ ∈ B, centralCharacter χ x ∉ idealImage M
blocks.docstring:
The central character $\lambda_B$ of the block `B` does not vanish on the class sum of the
conjugacy class of `x`: for every `χ ∈ B`, the algebraic integer $\omega_\chi(\hat K)$ does not
lie in `M`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«9.23».IsNonvanishingClass
justification.why_needed: λ_B(K̂) ≠ 0, the condition on conjugacy classes used to define defect groups.

blocks.name: IsNonvanishingClass
blocks.text:
/-- The central character $\lambda_B$ of the block `B` does not vanish on the class sum of the
conjugacy class of `x`: for every `χ ∈ B`, the algebraic integer $\omega_\chi(\hat K)$ does not
lie in `M`. -/
def IsNonvanishingClass (B : Set (G → ℂ)) (x : G) : Prop :=
  ∀ χ ∈ B, centralCharacter χ x ∉ idealImage M

blocks.docstring:
`D` is a defect group of the conjugacy class of `x`: a Sylow `p`-subgroup of the
centraliser $C_G(x)$, regarded as a subgroup of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Sylow p ↥(Subgroup.centralizer {x}) with Subgroup.map (used to define it)
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.23».IsDefectGroupOfClass
justification.why_needed: Defect group δ(K) of a conjugacy class: a Sylow p-subgroup of C_G(x), as a subgroup of G. Mathlib's `Sylow p H` is for a group H, not for 'Sylow subgroup of a subgroup of G, viewed in G'.

blocks.name: IsDefectGroupOfClass
blocks.text:
/-- `D` is a defect group of the conjugacy class of `x`: a Sylow `p`-subgroup of the
centraliser $C_G(x)$, regarded as a subgroup of `G`. -/
def IsDefectGroupOfClass (p : ℕ) (x : G) (D : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : Sylow p (Subgroup.centralizer {x}),
    D = (P : Subgroup (Subgroup.centralizer {x})).map (Subgroup.centralizer {x}).subtype

blocks.code:
def IsDefectGroup (p : ℕ) (B : Set (G → ℂ)) (D : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  (∃ x : G, IsNonvanishingClass M B x ∧ IsDefectGroupOfClass p x D) ∧
    ∀ (y : G) (Q : Subgroup G), IsNonvanishingClass M B y → IsDefectGroupOfClass p y Q →
      Nat.card D ≤ Nat.card Q
blocks.docstring:
`D` is a defect group of the block `B`: a defect group of a conjugacy class $K$ with
$\lambda_B(\hat K) \neq 0$, of smallest order among all such defect groups (Brauer's min–max
theorem). The class of the identity always satisfies $\lambda_B(\hat 1) = 1 \neq 0$, so defect
groups exist, and they form a single conjugacy class of $p$-subgroups of `G`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«9.23».IsDefectGroup
justification.why_needed: Defect groups of a block are absent from Mathlib; defined via Brauer's min–max theorem.

blocks.name: IsDefectGroup
blocks.text:
/-- `D` is a defect group of the block `B`: a defect group of a conjugacy class $K$ with
$\lambda_B(\hat K) \neq 0$, of smallest order among all such defect groups (Brauer's min–max
theorem). The class of the identity always satisfies $\lambda_B(\hat 1) = 1 \neq 0$, so defect
groups exist, and they form a single conjugacy class of $p$-subgroups of `G`. -/
def IsDefectGroup (p : ℕ) (B : Set (G → ℂ)) (D : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  (∃ x : G, IsNonvanishingClass M B x ∧ IsDefectGroupOfClass p x D) ∧
    ∀ (y : G) (Q : Subgroup G), IsNonvanishingClass M B y → IsDefectGroupOfClass p y Q →
      Nat.card D ≤ Nat.card Q

blocks.docstring:
The character `χ` has height zero with respect to the prime `p` and the defect group `D` of
its block: $\chi(1)_p \cdot |D| = |G|_p$, i.e. $
u_p(\chi(1)) + 
u_p(|D|) = 
u_p(|G|)$.

justification.name: Kourovka.«9.23».HasHeightZero
justification.why_needed: Heights of irreducible characters in a block are absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: HasHeightZero
blocks.text:
/-- The character `χ` has height zero with respect to the prime `p` and the defect group `D` of
its block: $\chi(1)_p \cdot |D| = |G|_p$, i.e. $\nu_p(\chi(1)) + \nu_p(|D|) = \nu_p(|G|)$. -/
def HasHeightZero (p : ℕ) (D : Subgroup G) (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, χ 1 = n ∧
    padicValNat p n + padicValNat p (Nat.card D) = padicValNat p (Nat.card G)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsIrreducibleCharacter.one_ne_zero {χ : G → ℂ} (h : IsIrreducibleCharacter χ) :
    χ 1 ≠ 0 := by
  obtain ⟨V, hV, rfl⟩ := h
  rw [FDRep.char_one]
  have := Simple.not_isZero V
  norm_cast
  intro h0
  apply this
  have hsub : Subsingleton V := Module.finrank_zero_iff.mp h0
  rw [Limits.IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero]
  ext x
  exact hsub.elim _ _
blocks.docstring: An irreducible character has nonzero degree.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem centralCharacter_one {χ : G → ℂ} (hχ : χ 1 ≠ 0) : centralCharacter χ 1 = 1 := by
  have h : Subgroup.centralizer ({1} : Set G) = ⊤ :=
    eq_top_iff.mpr fun g _ => by simp [Subgroup.mem_centralizer_iff]
  simp [centralCharacter, h, Subgroup.index_top, hχ]
blocks.docstring: The central character value at the identity is $\omega_\chi(\hat 1) = 1$.
blocks.name: centralCharacter_one

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem sameBlock_refl (χ : G → ℂ) : SameBlock M χ χ :=
  fun _ => ⟨0, M.zero_mem, by simp⟩
blocks.name: sameBlock_refl
blocks.text:
/-- `SameBlock M` is reflexive. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem sameBlock_refl (χ : G → ℂ) : SameBlock M χ χ :=
  fun _ => ⟨0, M.zero_mem, by simp⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem SameBlock.symm {χ ψ : G → ℂ} (h : SameBlock M χ ψ) : SameBlock M ψ χ := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrx⟩ := h x
  exact ⟨-r, M.neg_mem hr, by rw [Subalgebra.coe_neg, hrx]; ring⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBlock.subset_isIrreducibleCharacter {B : Set (G → ℂ)} (hB : IsBlock M B) :
    ∀ χ ∈ B, IsIrreducibleCharacter χ := by
  obtain ⟨χ, -, rfl⟩ := hB
  exact fun _ h => h.1
blocks.docstring: A block consists of irreducible characters.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBlock.nonempty {B : Set (G → ℂ)} (hB : IsBlock M B) : B.Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨χ, hχ, rfl⟩ := hB
  exact ⟨χ, hχ, sameBlock_refl M χ⟩

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBlock.isNonvanishingClass_one (hM : M ≠ ⊤) {B : Set (G → ℂ)} (hB : IsBlock M B) :
    IsNonvanishingClass M B 1 := by
  intro χ hχ
  rw [centralCharacter_one (hB.subset_isIrreducibleCharacter χ hχ).one_ne_zero]
  rintro ⟨a, haM, ha⟩
  apply hM
  rw [Ideal.eq_top_iff_one]
  have : a = 1 := Subtype.ext (by simpa using ha)
  exact this ▸ haM
blocks.docstring:
The class of the identity is nonvanishing for every block (when `M` is a proper ideal), so
every block has a nonvanishing class and hence a defect group.
blocks.name: IsBlock.isNonvanishingClass_one
blocks.text:
variable {M} in
/-- The class of the identity is nonvanishing for every block (when `M` is a proper ideal), so
every block has a nonvanishing class and hence a defect group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBlock.isNonvanishingClass_one (hM : M ≠ ⊤) {B : Set (G → ℂ)} (hB : IsBlock M B) :
    IsNonvanishingClass M B 1 := by
  intro χ hχ
  rw [centralCharacter_one (hB.subset_isIrreducibleCharacter χ hχ).one_ne_zero]
  rintro ⟨a, haM, ha⟩
  apply hM
  rw [Ideal.eq_top_iff_one]
  have : a = 1 := Subtype.ext (by simpa using ha)
  exact this ▸ haM
end Definitions

all defect groups of $B$; a character $\chi \in B$ has height $0$ when $\chi(1)_p |D| = |G|_p$.

blocks.docstring:
c) (R. Brauer) For every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ and every $p$-block $B$ of $G$ with
defect group $D(B)$: $D(B)$ is abelian if and only if $k_0(B) = k(B)$, i.e. if and only if every
irreducible complex character in $B$ has height $0$.

This is Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture. The implication "$D(B)$ abelian
$\Rightarrow k_0(B) = k(B)$" was proved by R. Kessar and G. Malle (2013) and the converse
"$k_0(B) = k(B) \Rightarrow D(B)$ abelian" by G. Malle, G. Navarro, A. A. Schaeffer Fry and
P. H. Tiep (2024).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.23

by V. D. Mazurov

Let $G$ be a finite group, $B$ a block of characters of $G$, $D(B)$ its defect group and
$k(B)$ (respectively, $k_0(B)$) the number of all irreducible complex characters (of height $0$)
lying in $B$. *Conjectures:*

a) (R. Brauer) $k(B) \leq |D(B)|$; this has been proved for $p$-soluble groups
(D. Gluck, K. Magaard, U. Riese, P. Schmid, *J. Algebra*, **279** (2004), 694–719);

b) (J. B. Olsson) $k_0(B) \leq |D(B) : D(B)'|$, where $D(B)'$ is the derived subgroup of
$D(B)$;

c) (R. Brauer) $D(B)$ is abelian if and only if $k_0(B) = k(B)$.

Part c) is Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture. It is not starred in the notebook, but it is now a
theorem: the direction "$D(B)$ abelian $\Rightarrow k_0(B) = k(B)$" was proved by Kessar and
Malle (2013), and the converse by Malle, Navarro, Schaeffer Fry and Tiep (2024). Parts a) and b)
are open.

## Formalisation

Here "block" means $p$-block for a prime $p$; the statements are quantified over $p$, $G$ and
$B$. Mathlib has no block theory, so this file sets up Brauer's character-theoretic definitions
(Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Chapter 15; Navarro, *Characters and Blocks of
Finite Groups*, Chapters 3 and 4). Let $\mathbf{R}$ be the ring of all algebraic integers in
$\mathbb{C}$ (`integralClosure ℤ ℂ`) and $M$ a maximal ideal of $\mathbf{R}$ containing $p$.

* The irreducible complex characters of $G$ are the characters of the simple objects of
  `FDRep ℂ G`.
* For an irreducible character $\chi$ and $x \in G$ with conjugacy class $K$, the central
  character value $\omega_\chi(\hat K) = |K| \chi(x) / \chi(1) = |G : C_G(x)| \chi(x) / \chi(1)$
  is an algebraic integer. Two irreducible characters $\chi, \psi$ lie in the same $p$-block if
  and only if $\omega_\chi(\hat K) \equiv \omega_\psi(\hat K) \pmod M$ for every conjugacy
  class $K$; the $p$-blocks are the equivalence classes of this relation. The resulting
  partition does not depend on the choice of $M$; the statements below quantify over all
  admissible $M$.
* A block $B$ has a central character $\lambda_B$ with $\lambda_B(\hat K) = \omega_\chi(\hat K)
  \bmod M$ for any $\chi \in B$. The defect groups of a class $K = x^G$ are the Sylow
  $p$-subgroups $\delta(K)$ of $C_G(x)$. By Brauer's min–max theorem, the defect groups of $B$
  are exactly the groups $\delta(K)$ of smallest order among the classes $K$ with
  $\lambda_B(\hat K) \neq 0$; they form a single conjugacy class of $p$-subgroups of $G$. This
  characterisation is taken as the definition of a defect group $D(B)$.
* If $|G|_p = p^a$ and $|D(B)| = p^d$, every $\chi \in B$ has $\chi(1)_p = p^{a - d + h}$ for an
  integer $h \geq 0$, the *height* of $\chi$. So $\chi$ has height $0$ if and only if
  $\chi(1)_p |D(B)| = |G|_p$.

Since all defect groups of $B$ are conjugate, $|D(B)|$, $|D(B) : D(B)'|$ and whether $D(B)$ is
abelian are well defined, and the statements quantify over every defect group of $B$. The solved
special case of a) for $p$-soluble groups is only mentioned in the docstring.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 9.23.
* D. Gluck, K. Magaard, U. Riese, P. Schmid, *The solution of the k(GV)-problem*,
  [J. Algebra 279 (2004), 694–719](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2004.02.027).
* R. Kessar, G. Malle, *Quasi-isolated blocks and Brauer's height zero conjecture*,
  [Ann. of Math. 178 (2013), 321–384](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2013.178.1.6).
* G. Malle, G. Navarro, A. A. Schaeffer Fry, P. H. Tiep, *Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture*,
  [Ann. of Math. 200 (2024), 557–608](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2024.200.2.4).
-/

open CategoryTheory

namespace Kourovka.«9.23»

section Definitions

variable {G : Type} [Group G]

/-- A function `χ : G → ℂ` is an irreducible complex character of `G` if it is the character
of a simple, i.e. irreducible, finite-dimensional complex representation of `G`. -/
def IsIrreducibleCharacter (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ V : FDRep ℂ G, Simple V ∧ V.character = χ

/-- The central character value $\omega_\chi(\hat K) = |K| \chi(x) / \chi(1)$ of `χ` at the
conjugacy class $K$ of `x`, where $|K| = |G : C_G(x)|$. For an irreducible character `χ` this is
an algebraic integer. -/
noncomputable def centralCharacter (χ : G → ℂ) (x : G) : ℂ :=
  ((Subgroup.centralizer {x}).index : ℂ) * χ x / χ 1

variable (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ))

/-- The set of complex numbers lying in the ideal `M` of the ring of algebraic integers. -/
def idealImage : Set ℂ :=
  Subtype.val '' (M : Set (integralClosure ℤ ℂ))

/-- `χ` and `ψ` lie in the same block with respect to the maximal ideal `M` of the algebraic
integers: $\omega_\chi(\hat K) \equiv \omega_\psi(\hat K) \pmod M$ for every conjugacy class
$K$ of `G`. -/
def SameBlock (χ ψ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : G, centralCharacter χ x - centralCharacter ψ x ∈ idealImage M

/-- `B` is a block of characters of `G` with respect to the maximal ideal `M` (a $p$-block, where
$p$ is the prime in `M`): an equivalence class of irreducible characters of `G` under
`SameBlock M`. -/
def IsBlock (B : Set (G → ℂ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ χ, IsIrreducibleCharacter χ ∧ B = {ψ | IsIrreducibleCharacter ψ ∧ SameBlock M χ ψ}

/-- The central character $\lambda_B$ of the block `B` does not vanish on the class sum of the
conjugacy class of `x`: for every `χ ∈ B`, the algebraic integer $\omega_\chi(\hat K)$ does not
lie in `M`. -/
def IsNonvanishingClass (B : Set (G → ℂ)) (x : G) : Prop :=
  ∀ χ ∈ B, centralCharacter χ x ∉ idealImage M

/-- `D` is a defect group of the conjugacy class of `x`: a Sylow `p`-subgroup of the
centraliser $C_G(x)$, regarded as a subgroup of `G`. -/
def IsDefectGroupOfClass (p : ℕ) (x : G) (D : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : Sylow p (Subgroup.centralizer {x}),
    D = (P : Subgroup (Subgroup.centralizer {x})).map (Subgroup.centralizer {x}).subtype

/-- `D` is a defect group of the block `B`: a defect group of a conjugacy class $K$ with
$\lambda_B(\hat K) \neq 0$, of smallest order among all such defect groups (Brauer's min–max
theorem). The class of the identity always satisfies $\lambda_B(\hat 1) = 1 \neq 0$, so defect
groups exist, and they form a single conjugacy class of $p$-subgroups of `G`. -/
def IsDefectGroup (p : ℕ) (B : Set (G → ℂ)) (D : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  (∃ x : G, IsNonvanishingClass M B x ∧ IsDefectGroupOfClass p x D) ∧
    ∀ (y : G) (Q : Subgroup G), IsNonvanishingClass M B y → IsDefectGroupOfClass p y Q →
      Nat.card D ≤ Nat.card Q

/-- The character `χ` has height zero with respect to the prime `p` and the defect group `D` of
its block: $\chi(1)_p \cdot |D| = |G|_p$, i.e. $\nu_p(\chi(1)) + \nu_p(|D|) = \nu_p(|G|)$. -/
def HasHeightZero (p : ℕ) (D : Subgroup G) (χ : G → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, χ 1 = n ∧
    padicValNat p n + padicValNat p (Nat.card D) = padicValNat p (Nat.card G)

/-- An irreducible character has nonzero degree. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsIrreducibleCharacter.one_ne_zero {χ : G → ℂ} (h : IsIrreducibleCharacter χ) :
    χ 1 ≠ 0 := by
  obtain ⟨V, hV, rfl⟩ := h
  rw [FDRep.char_one]
  have := Simple.not_isZero V
  norm_cast
  intro h0
  apply this
  have hsub : Subsingleton V := Module.finrank_zero_iff.mp h0
  rw [Limits.IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero]
  ext x
  exact hsub.elim _ _

/-- The central character value at the identity is $\omega_\chi(\hat 1) = 1$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem centralCharacter_one {χ : G → ℂ} (hχ : χ 1 ≠ 0) : centralCharacter χ 1 = 1 := by
  have h : Subgroup.centralizer ({1} : Set G) = ⊤ :=
    eq_top_iff.mpr fun g _ => by simp [Subgroup.mem_centralizer_iff]
  simp [centralCharacter, h, Subgroup.index_top, hχ]

/-- `SameBlock M` is reflexive. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem sameBlock_refl (χ : G → ℂ) : SameBlock M χ χ :=
  fun _ => ⟨0, M.zero_mem, by simp⟩

variable {M} in
/-- `SameBlock M` is symmetric. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem SameBlock.symm {χ ψ : G → ℂ} (h : SameBlock M χ ψ) : SameBlock M ψ χ := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrx⟩ := h x
  exact ⟨-r, M.neg_mem hr, by rw [Subalgebra.coe_neg, hrx]; ring⟩

variable {M} in
/-- A block consists of irreducible characters. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBlock.subset_isIrreducibleCharacter {B : Set (G → ℂ)} (hB : IsBlock M B) :
    ∀ χ ∈ B, IsIrreducibleCharacter χ := by
  obtain ⟨χ, -, rfl⟩ := hB
  exact fun _ h => h.1

variable {M} in
/-- A block is nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBlock.nonempty {B : Set (G → ℂ)} (hB : IsBlock M B) : B.Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨χ, hχ, rfl⟩ := hB
  exact ⟨χ, hχ, sameBlock_refl M χ⟩

variable {M} in
/-- The class of the identity is nonvanishing for every block (when `M` is a proper ideal), so
every block has a nonvanishing class and hence a defect group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBlock.isNonvanishingClass_one (hM : M ≠ ⊤) {B : Set (G → ℂ)} (hB : IsBlock M B) :
    IsNonvanishingClass M B 1 := by
  intro χ hχ
  rw [centralCharacter_one (hB.subset_isIrreducibleCharacter χ hχ).one_ne_zero]
  rintro ⟨a, haM, ha⟩
  apply hM
  rw [Ideal.eq_top_iff_one]
  have : a = 1 := Subtype.ext (by simpa using ha)
  exact this ▸ haM

end Definitions

/--
a) (R. Brauer) For every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ and every $p$-block $B$ of $G$ with
defect group $D(B)$, one has $k(B) \leq |D(B)|$, where $k(B)$ is the number of irreducible
complex characters lying in $B$.

This is Brauer's $k(B)$-conjecture. The Kourovka Notebook records that it has been proved for
$p$-soluble groups by D. Gluck, K. Magaard, U. Riese and P. Schmid (*J. Algebra* **279** (2004),
694–719).

Here $M$ ranges over all maximal ideals of the algebraic integers containing $p$ (this fixes the
reduction modulo $p$ used to define blocks) and $D$ over all defect groups of $B$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.23».parts.a (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ)) (hM : M.IsMaximal) (hp : (p : integralClosure ℤ ℂ) ∈ M)
    (B : Set (G → ℂ)) (hB : IsBlock M B) (D : Subgroup G) (hD : IsDefectGroup M p B D) :
    B.ncard ≤ Nat.card D := by
  sorry

/--
b) (J. B. Olsson) For every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ and every $p$-block $B$ of $G$ with
defect group $D(B)$, one has $k_0(B) \leq |D(B) : D(B)'|$, where $k_0(B)$ is the number of
irreducible complex characters of height $0$ lying in $B$ and $D(B)'$ is the derived subgroup of
$D(B)$.

Here $M$ ranges over all maximal ideals of the algebraic integers containing $p$ and $D$ over
all defect groups of $B$; a character $\chi \in B$ has height $0$ when $\chi(1)_p |D| = |G|_p$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.23».parts.b (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ)) (hM : M.IsMaximal) (hp : (p : integralClosure ℤ ℂ) ∈ M)
    (B : Set (G → ℂ)) (hB : IsBlock M B) (D : Subgroup G) (hD : IsDefectGroup M p B D) :
    {χ ∈ B | HasHeightZero p D χ}.ncard ≤ (commutator D).index := by
  sorry

/--
c) (R. Brauer) For every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ and every $p$-block $B$ of $G$ with
defect group $D(B)$: $D(B)$ is abelian if and only if $k_0(B) = k(B)$, i.e. if and only if every
irreducible complex character in $B$ has height $0$.

This is Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture. The implication "$D(B)$ abelian
$\Rightarrow k_0(B) = k(B)$" was proved by R. Kessar and G. Malle (2013) and the converse
"$k_0(B) = k(B) \Rightarrow D(B)$ abelian" by G. Malle, G. Navarro, A. A. Schaeffer Fry and
P. H. Tiep (2024).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.23».parts.c (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (M : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ ℂ)) (hM : M.IsMaximal) (hp : (p : integralClosure ℤ ℂ) ∈ M)
    (B : Set (G → ℂ)) (hB : IsBlock M B) (D : Subgroup G) (hD : IsDefectGroup M p B D) :
    IsMulCommutative D ↔ {χ ∈ B | HasHeightZero p D χ}.ncard = B.ncard := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.23»

items: Blocks are defined character-theoretically à la Brauer/Isaacs (Ch. 15)/Navarro (Ch. 3): fix a maximal ideal M of the ring of all algebraic integers `integralClosure ℤ ℂ` with p ∈ M; χ, ψ ∈ Irr(G) are in the same block iff ω_χ(K̂) − ω_ψ(K̂) ∈ M for every class K, with ω_χ(K̂) = |G:C_G(x)|·χ(x)/χ(1). The statements quantify over all such M. (The partition is in fact independent of M: the block idempotent coefficients (1/|G|)Σ_{χ∈B}χ(1)χ(x⁻¹) = (1/|G|)Σ_T Φ_T(1)φ_T(x⁻¹) are p-integral at every prime over p since |G|_p | Φ_T(1); either way, quantifying over M is faithful.)

Congruences use the idiom `∃ r ∈ M, (r : ℂ) = a − b` and `∃ r ∉ M, (r : ℂ) = ω_χ(x)`, which relies on the standard theorem that central character values ω_χ(K̂) are algebraic integers; a reviewer should confirm they are happy with this encoding.

Defect group of B is defined via Brauer's min–max theorem: D is a Sylow p-subgroup of C_G(x) (image of a Mathlib `Sylow p (centralizer {x})` under the subtype map) for some x with λ_B(x̂) ≠ 0 (i.e. ω_χ(x̂) ∉ M for χ ∈ B), of minimal order among all such. This is equivalent to the textbook definitions (defect classes / minimal D with e_B ∈ (kG)^G_D) but is not literally one of them; it never degenerates because the class of 1 always has λ_B(1̂) = 1.

Height zero is defined literally as χ(1)_p·|D| = |G|_p via `padicValNat p n + padicValNat p (Nat.card D) = padicValNat p (Nat.card G)` with `χ 1 = (n : ℂ)` (following the table notes), rather than via minimality of ν_p(χ(1)) within B.

Irreducible characters are functions `G → ℂ` of the form `V.character` for a `Simple V : FDRep ℂ G`; k(B) and k_0(B) are `Nat.card` of the corresponding sets of functions (distinct simple representations have distinct characters, so this counts irreducible characters). Because `FDRep` needs the group and the field in the same universe, G is quantified over `Type`.
|D(B):D(B)'| is formalised as `(commutator ↥D).index`, and 'D(B) abelian' as `IsMulCommutative ↥D`.

Category tags: a) and b) `research open`; c) `research solved` as instructed. Three short proved `category API` lemmas (reflexivity/symmetry of SameBlock, ω_χ(1̂) = 1) are included as basic sanity tests of the definitions.

reviewer_notes: Bail-outs c02, c04, c05, c06 claimed p-blocks/defect groups/heights are 'missing primitives'. This is refuted by c01/c03/c07/c08: blocks and defect groups have a purely character-theoretic definition (Brauer/Isaacs Ch. 15, Navarro Ch. 3–4) expressible with FDRep characters and the ring of algebraic integers, and the four files do it faithfully. Modeling caveats a reviewer should be aware of (all standard theorems, not extra hypotheses): (1) the block partition is quantified over every maximal ideal M ∋ p of the algebraic integers; it is in fact M-independent (block idempotents are p-integral at every prime over p), and even if it were not, the literature's 'p-block' is relative to such a fixed M, so ∀ M is exactly the intended claim; (2) 'D is a defect group of B' is Brauer's min–max characterisation (Sylow p-subgroup of C_G(x) of smallest order among classes with λ_B(K̂) ≠ 0), which I re-derived to be equivalent to the textbook defect groups; (3) ¬(ω_χ(x) ∈ image M) reads as λ_B(K̂) ≠ 0 because ω_χ(K̂) is an algebraic integer; (4) irreducible characters are characters of Simple objects of FDRep ℂ G, forcing G : Type (universe 0), consistent with other Kourovka files; (5) Set.ncard is used on sets that are mathematically finite (subsets of Irr(G)). statement_tex:
Let $G$ be a finite group, $B$ a block of
characters of $ G$, $D(B)$ its defect group and $k(B)$
(respectively, $k_0(B)$) the number of all irreducible complex
characters (of height 0) lying in $B$. {\it Conjectures:}

\makebox[25pt][r]{a)} (R.\,Brauer) \ $k(B) \leq |D(B)|$; this has
been proved for $p\hs$-soluble groups (D.\,Gluck, K.\,Magaard,
U.\,Riese, P.\,Schmid, {\it J.~Algebra}, \textbf{279} (2004), 694--719);

\makebox[25pt][r]{b)} (J.\,B.\,Olsson) \ $k_0(B) \leq |D(B) :
D(B)'|$, where $D(B)'$ is the derived subgroup of $D(B)$;

\makebox[25pt][r]{c)} (R.\,Brauer) \ $D(B)$
is abelian if
and only
if $k_0(B)=k(B)$.
title: Conjecture 9.23
